RAD-149.plan: Calm/Chaos hold deck. Units played to battlefields you control enter ready, so Riven deploys a unit and immediately exhausts it to pay for other cards. She anchors one battlefield, stuns attackers, and protects her spells with Calm counterplay, then side-decks to beat whatever the room is playing.
builds: Hold/control: sit on one battlefield, pay exhaust costs with fresh units, stun anything that attacks.
Two-front pressure: removal and ready effects to contest the second battlefield and conquer.
Single-battlefield race: focus one battlefield and score faster than the opponent.
strengths: Best legend in the Radiance format per tournament results: 5 wins and 16 top cuts in the first two weeks, including Orlando $25k and Convergence IV.
Very strong battlefield control; fresh units double as resources.
Side deck adapts to the field.
weaknesses: Loses to synergies she did not side-board for.
Running little gear removal opens the door for gear decks like Jayce.
Tuning against Aurora decks weakens her Kai'Sa and Kennen matchups.
vs: Bring a gear-centric threat: Jayce posts about 64% into Riven because she cuts gear removal.
Do not fight her on one battlefield; spread pressure so her stuns and exhaust costs are stretched.
Master Yi, Rek'Sai and Kha'Zix have posted winning records into her; small samples.
Kill or bounce the units she deploys before she can exhaust them for value.
RAD-149.banImpact: Nov 23 bans hit this deck hardest: Riven - Broken Blade (the usual Chosen Champion), Zhonya's Hourglass, Stellacorn Herder, Emperor's Dais and Star Spring are all banned. Riot cited Riven at 43% of European Regional decks with 3 of the top 4. The Legend itself is not banned; the other Riven champions are Riven - Deserter and Riven - Shattered. Every tournament list in this app is pre-ban.

OGN-247.plan: Fury/Mind spell tempo. Removal clears the way so low-might units with strong abilities can conquer most turns. If early scoring is stopped, she pivots to a slower value game of removal plus card draw.
builds: Tempo conquer: early removal, accelerate big threats to conquer immediately.
Value pivot: hold removal and draw, close with the top-end units.
strengths: About 58% win rate in early Radiance; 12 top cuts in two weeks.
Deep removal suite and draw.
Flexible late game through OGN-116 and damage spells.
weaknesses: Low-might units lose even trades and die to cheap removal.
Spell-heavy turns can empty her hand.
Slows down badly when early scoring is denied.
vs: Deny the early conquers; her clock depends on scoring early.
Make her trade removal for small units, then land a bigger threat she cannot burn.
Lillia has posted 64% into Kai'Sa in early data; Kha'Zix struggles badly (2-6).
OGN-247.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Brynhir Thundersong (3 in the list in this app) is banned.

VEN-155.plan: Chaos/Order off-tempo value. Holds the opponent off early, then develops in bursts using cheap self-milling units (OGN-194, OGN-195 from the trash) and lots of discard-then-draw. Kennen's legend empowers when you play cards from anywhere other than your hand, and turns that into Assault 2 for conquers.
builds: Miracle/trash core with OGN-194 and OGN-195 (most common).
Baited Hook or Deathknell variants were tested in Vendetta.
strengths: About 59% win rate, best of the non-Riven legends in early Radiance.
Very hard to run out of cards.
Slightly favored into Riven (51-49).
weaknesses: Burst development means some turns are weak on board.
Sideboards are currently tuned for Kai'Sa, leaving gaps.
vs: Trash hate and banish effects shut off the free replays.
Pressure early before the trash fills (about ten cards powers OGN-195).
Rengar struggles here (28%); Akali (53%) and Kai'Sa (52%) are slightly favored.
VEN-155.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Nocturne, Horrifying and Rhasa the Sunderer (3 of each in the Singapore top-8 list) are banned. That list also ran Stacked Deck, which was already banned in September. Kennen is not banned in 2v2.

VEN-149.plan: Mind/Body big-unit deck. Fetch and cheat out UNL-118 early with OGN-160 and OGN-115 to take a battlefield, with UNL-088 as a backup win condition in long games.
builds: Gear build around VEN-075 was dropped because gear removal is common.
strengths: About 58% win rate and 64% into Riven.
Second win condition in UNL-088.
weaknesses: Few tricks beyond the main threat.
Gear removal in sideboards hurts.
Weak into Kai'Sa and Kennen.
vs: Save hard removal for UNL-118; the deck folds when it is answered.
Pack gear removal for game 2 and 3.
Race it: the setup costs early turns.
VEN-149.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Dazzling Aurora (3 in both Jayce lists in this app) is banned.

OGS-019.plan: Calm/Body hold-or-conquer. A lone defender gets +2 might, forcing the opponent to over-commit to break a battlefield. Cheap spells relocate or remove enemies while draw units keep the hand full.
builds: Hold-first tempo (the established list since Unleashed).
strengths: 67-33 into Riven in early data.
Strong early board and card flow; great in best-of-one and smaller events.
weaknesses: Needs about 10 wins in long events, which exposes poor matchups.
Weak into Kennen and Kai'Sa.
Note: this legend is banned in 2v2.
vs: Attack with two units or a unit plus a trick so the lone-defender bonus does not matter.
Let him hold one battlefield while you score the other faster.
Removal that ignores might (stun, bounce) sidesteps the +2.

SFD-195.plan: Calm/Chaos value with timing. Irelia readies chosen units and controls the pace, then wins with SFD-057 dominating the board or SFD-048 filling the hand. VEN-044 holds a battlefield late.
builds: One core value list with matchup-specific add-ins.
strengths: High ceiling; won the Wuhan regional and was Top 2 at Convergence IV.
Flexible answers for big Body and Fury threats.
weaknesses: About 44% win rate in early Radiance; loses to most higher-tier legends except Vex.
Struggles in fast metas.
vs: Play fast; she wants long, value-oriented games.
Answer SFD-057, SFD-048 or VEN-044 before they snowball, but expect a Calm or Chaos protection spell in response.

UNL-183.plan: Fury/Body aggro. Win the first showdowns with 3-might attackers, hide the real board with Ambush, keep threats coming, and draw enough to not run out.
builds: Shared early game and spell package; spell counts vary.
strengths: Top aggressive legend of Vendetta; strong early tempo.
Ambush makes defending guesswork.
weaknesses: Few comeback tools once behind.
Poor into Riven (31%) and Kennen (28%).
vs: Survive the first two turns; hold cheap removal for the early 3-might attackers.
Keep a reaction open when defending, Ambush units can join showdowns.
Once you stabilize, he has little to recover with.

VEN-139.plan: Fury/Calm value control. Stabilize the early board, then land must-answer units such as VEN-044 and protect them with Calm spells while drawing heavily. Gets stronger the more you try to remove her units.
strengths: About 52% with few bad matchups.
Top 4 at the largest early Radiance event.
Slightly favored into Kennen (53%).
weaknesses: Slow start; her key 4-cost card is fragile.
Hard matchups into Kai'Sa and Riven.
vs: Pressure her before the engine is online.
Remove threats when she is tapped out of protection runes.
Do not feed her removal into a protection spell; bait it first.

SFD-187.plan: Fury/Order conquer deck that looks aggressive but plays off-tempo: cheap units build an early scoreboard lead, then Order removal handles threats. Her legend reveals the top 2 when you conquer and lets you play one.
builds: Typical lists: 3 SFD-175, at least nine 2-cost units, OGN-012.
strengths: Winning records into Kennen and Riven (small sample, about 80 games, 54%).
Punishes over-commitment and tapped-out opponents.
weaknesses: Bad from behind.
Many legends match her early game.
vs: Contest the early conquers so she never gets the lead.
Keep runes up; she punishes opponents who tap out.
Do not over-commit units into her removal.

UNL-201.plan: Body/Chaos midrange. Cheap units gain XP and claim battlefields, then 4- and 5-cost threats take over with Ambush tricks and disruption. Spends XP to buff or rescue units.
strengths: Favored into Riven (57%) and Kennen (58%) in early data.
Flexible pressure, keeps opponents guessing.
weaknesses: 2-6 against Kai'Sa.
Slow against Aurora decks; lacks value against Azir; struggled against Annie.
vs: Kill early units before they win combats (each win gives XP).
Out-value him in a long game; he runs out of steam.
UNL-201.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Star Spring (1 in the list in this app) is banned.

OGN-265.plan: Mind/Order token control. Make a 1-might Recruit every turn and use tokens to conquer empty battlefields rather than fight. Removal, stun and might reduction take early scoreboard control.
strengths: Steady unit generation; strong removal.
Recent Top 8 at Convergence IV.
weaknesses: 42% early Radiance win rate; about twice as many bad matchups as good.
1-might tokens lose any real fight.
vs: Never leave a battlefield empty; tokens only score on open ground.
Area damage or might reduction wipes the token board.

OGN-269.plan: Body/Order buff aggro: score at all costs. Buffs win combats and the legend saves a buffed unit from dying by recalling it. Disruption and ready effects keep scoring every turn.
builds: Sustained: battlefields for recovery plus OGN-156 hand attack.
strengths: Snowballs when ahead; units are hard to kill for good.
weaknesses: No natural card draw.
17% into Riven in early data.
Falls off in long games.
vs: Remove units before they are buffed, or exile/bounce instead of killing (his save only stops death).
Go long; Sett runs out of cards.

UNL-199.plan: Mind/Order Deathknell value. Temporary Reflection copies die and trigger Deathknells for draws, runes, units or removal. Snowballs mid-game or out-values.
builds: Western: OGN-242 tempo with late bombs.
Chinese: slower, more removal (OGN-209) and UNL-209 draw.
strengths: Very hard to out-value once UNL-172 and OGN-236 are down.
53% with only 9 unfavorable matchups.
weaknesses: Narrow build-around; weak in Chaos-heavy metas where units are bounced instead of killed.
36% into Riven.
vs: Bounce or banish instead of kill; Deathknell needs units to die.
Answer OGN-236 before its Deathknell can matter.

SFD-199.plan: Mind/Chaos attrition lock. Stall with removal and disruptive units, never run out of cards thanks to the legend, then loop bounce-and-replay engines and strip the opponent's hand.
strengths: Strong inevitability in long games.
weaknesses: Weak early board.
Unfavorable into Riven and Kennen.
vs: Develop units fast and score before the engine is online.
Do not let the game stall.

UNL-189.plan: Calm/Mind Sprite tokens. Trade Temporary 3-might Sprites for real units, then conquer; if the opponent avoids fights, she gets free conquers.
strengths: 64% into Kai'Sa in early tournament data.
Free conquers when opponents won't trade.
weaknesses: Low raw might; loses to Riven and Kennen.
vs: Use units bigger than 3 might to hold battlefields.
Don't trade real units into Sprites; they die on their own.

SFD-197.plan: Calm/Order equipment and Sand Soldier swarm. Cheap gear lets Azir make a 2-might Sand Soldier each turn; Weaponmaster equips them. Against fast decks he switches to stun and removal. SFD-198 is the late finisher.
builds: 13+ cheap equipment with Calm support spells.
strengths: Was a top-5 legend in Unleashed and Vendetta.
weaknesses: 46% in early Radiance, much weaker than before.
vs: Gear removal cuts off soldier production (he needs an Equipment played that turn).
Answer the board before SFD-198 turns it into a lethal swing.

RAD-145.plan: Calm/Mind gear-to-unit deck. Each Main Phase, turn one expensive gear into a unit with might equal to its cost. Main target is RAD-068 sitting on a battlefield.
builds: Top-heavy gear core (3x SFD-084, RAD-068, RAD-146) with protection.
Deploy-gear side option with RAD-062 and RAD-033.
strengths: Signature gear is protected from gear removal.
weaknesses: 39% early Radiance win rate.
Slow on four runes; too many 5-drops; few units.
vs: Pressure early before the gears come online.
Remove the animated gear while it is a unit; it can be hit by unit removal.

OGN-267.plan: Body/Chaos ramp into big units, then give them Ganking to contest both battlefields.
builds: OGN-160 core, similar to the Unleashed list; RAD-079 or VEN-085 in the sideboard.
strengths: Ganking on any size unit; OGN-268 wipes token boards.
weaknesses: Few early-game tools.
vs: Pressure before the ramp lands.

RAD-151.plan: Mind/Order token control. Exhaust three units to discount spells; both champion units reward exhausted units. Flood tokens, exhaust for value.
strengths: Simple, consistent plan.
weaknesses: 41% early win rate; 0-14 into Riven.
Gear-based token makers die to gear removal; predictable.
vs: Gear removal and area damage on tokens.
Punish the turns she exhausts her board.

VEN-145.plan: Calm/Mind control into late game. Readies runes after playing something costing 7+, so he stabilizes early and slams big units later.
strengths: Hard to stop once in the late game.
weaknesses: Ability does nothing for the first three turns.
43% early Radiance; bad into most top legends except Vex.
vs: Pressure early and keep him from stabilizing.
Hold removal for the big threats; he relies on protection spells.

UNL-193.plan: Calm/Chaos hold control. Take a battlefield early, draw when holding, bounce or recall contesters and stun big attackers. VEN-044 is the late engine.
builds: Hold control; backup for players who cannot build Riven.
strengths: Strong interaction; 1 win and 6 top cuts early in Radiance.
weaknesses: About 53%; unfavorable into most top legends (15 bad matchups).
Weak early game.
vs: Take the early battlefield fight; she wants to hold first.
Pressure the second battlefield; she is built to anchor one.

UNL-197.plan: Mind/Chaos tempo. Cheap units and support spells (often effectively free through the legend's showdown energy) win early showdowns, then close with OGN-173 or bounce defensively.
strengths: Was the top new Unleashed legend; strong early tempo.
weaknesses: Not brute-force; struggles once a slower deck stabilizes.
vs: Stabilize early; her power is in winning the first showdowns.
Hold reactions for showdowns, where her extra energy matters.

SFD-185.plan: Fury/Chaos reactive midrange. Draw on combat wins; protect UNL-150 and OGN-039, then widen with cheap and Hidden units.
strengths: Snowballs once a key threat survives.
weaknesses: No strong early champion; struggles from behind and in long games.
vs: Fast pressure and early removal of 4-might threats.
Avoid giving him combat wins (each draws a card).

OGS-017.plan: Fury/Chaos aggressive scoring. Readies 2 runes each end of turn, so she spends on her turn and still holds reactions. Aims to conquer nearly every turn to 8 points.
builds: All-in scoring with a containment trio for big units.
strengths: Constant pressure; Origins-era Tier 1 in North America.
weaknesses: Attackers hold poorly; hand empties fast.
vs: Contest conquests every turn and make her hold.
One big unit forces her to spend her containment cards.

OGN-263.plan: Mind/Chaos hidden control. Strong early game, hide a card every turn, hold battlefields and disrupt with Chaos.
strengths: Consistent; bluffing forces risky plays.
weaknesses: Needs a strong early game; falls off when the meta slows.
vs: Respect hidden cards; attack where he has none.
Slow, bigger decks outlast his early tempo.

UNL-191.plan: Calm/Body XP midrange. Race to 6 XP (+1 might for all units) and 11 XP (units enter ready). UNL-059 is the main payoff.
strengths: Strong late game once leveled.
weaknesses: No legend effect early; vulnerable to removal that ignores size.
vs: Deny XP early by winning combats.
Snowball before Level 6.

VEN-143.plan: Fury/Chaos fast scoring with Flow and card draw; keeps playing from a near-empty hand. Empowers when banishing.
strengths: Consistent; good in best-of-one.
weaknesses: Limited deck-building flexibility.
vs: Stabilize the board early; he wants a fast race.

VEN-153.plan: Body/Order board deck: big units, remove units in the enemy base, ready units with the Legend.
builds: Midrange Empower with VEN-124 and VEN-086.
strengths: Strong board pressure.
weaknesses: Little card draw; weak in long games.
vs: Extend the game and out-value.

VEN-151.plan: Mind/Chaos value midrange with removal; signature VEN-152 makes showdowns hard to contest.
strengths: Removal and extra draw; multiple Vendetta top 8s.
weaknesses: No big wins yet.
vs: Watch units left in base and VEN-069/VEN-055 with her signature spell.

VEN-141.plan: Fury/Body high-variance tempo. Turn-one 4-cost threats via rune-recycling energy, then keep adding threats.
strengths: Explosive early 4-might units that are hard to remove.
weaknesses: Bad starts are hard to recover; recycles runes.
vs: Destroy Seals early.
Have a turn-two answer for a 4-might unit.

VEN-147.plan: Calm/Order showdown value. Provokes showdowns and keeps key units alive with Tank.
strengths: Most deck-building freedom Calm/Order has had.
weaknesses: Champion units look weak; Tank rarely matters.
vs: Remove the Tank unit first or ignore it with stun/bounce.

RAD-155.plan: Body/Order Deploy-gear conquer. Each Deploy gear lets Jarvan move a friendly unit to that battlefield, supporting conquers and rescuing stranded units.
builds: Unit-focused conquer with cheap Deploy gear (theorycraft).
strengths: Showdown control and movement.
weaknesses: Card draw is thin; few Deploy gears exist; power-cost heavy.
vs: Removal on OGN-164.
Gear removal limits movement.

RAD-141.plan: Fury/Chaos Bomb control. Bomb gear tokens damage units in showdowns to clear battlefields, then hold.
strengths: Flexible damage-based removal.
weaknesses: Early units lose to 2-might units; thin draw.
vs: Retreat units to base away from Bombs.
Win early showdowns against his small units.

RAD-153.plan: Body/Chaos Hidden deck. Hide most turns, reveal on your turn for draw; opponents must either challenge hidden battlefields or let her hold.
builds: Small hand, few runes, many 4-cost Chaos units; sideboard for spell removal.
strengths: Strong into beefy unit decks.
weaknesses: Spell-based removal decks; power costs strain her.
vs: Spell removal is better than big units.
Do not challenge hidden battlefields without a payoff.

RAD-139.plan: Fury/Mind replay combo. Start reactive with removal, then replay on-play units with the signature spell RAD-140 for explosive turns.
strengths: Explosive turns; lots of removal.
weaknesses: Slow reactive start.
vs: Pressure early before the combo turn.

RAD-147.plan: Calm/Body Shield deck that uses Shield offensively via the legend (Assault equal to Shield).
builds: Theorycraft only; may end up an Aurora legend.
strengths: Big might on both attack and defense.
weaknesses: Unproven synergy.
vs: Chaos/Order removal ignores might entirely.
RAD-147.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Dazzling Aurora, which this guide expected the deck to use, is banned.

RAD-143.plan: Fury/Order brute force. Banish units or gear from your trash to add power for units/gear; cheat out 7- and 9-cost champions.
strengths: Early huge champions.
weaknesses: Unproven; protect runes.
vs: Trash hate removes his fuel.
Answer OGN-242.
RAD-143.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Baited Hook, one of the builds in this guide, is banned.

OGN-251.plan: Fury/Chaos discard aggro. Empty your hand fast; the Legend refills when you have one or fewer cards.
strengths: Cheap efficient units and removal.
weaknesses: Burns through resources fast.
vs: Slow the game and control resources; she runs out.

OGN-249.plan: Fury/Body ramp. Play 5+ might units for extra runes, then stomp with huge units and Dazzling Aurora.
strengths: Very large units; OGN-161 has Deflect.
weaknesses: Slow champions; little reactive removal.
vs: Score early and bounce big units with cheap spells.
OGN-249.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Dazzling Aurora, named in this guide's game plan, is banned.

OGN-253.plan: Fury/Order early tempo. Wins early showdowns, sacrifices cheap units into bigger ones with Baited Hook, and removes threats with Order spells.
vs: Stop the early momentum.
Kill Baited Hook.
strengths: Fast tempo; snowballs.
weaknesses: Few comeback tools; vulnerable to gear removal.
OGN-253.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Baited Hook, named in this guide's game plan, is banned.

OGN-255.plan: Calm/Mind hold deck. The Legend weakens enemy attackers, so Ahri holds a battlefield, builds value with UNL-048, then uses battlefields like Star Spring to reposition and push the other battlefield.
strengths: Long-term value when holding.
Did better in the slower Chinese metagame.
weaknesses: Curve gap between 3 and 7 cost.
Has to keep runes open to stop conquers; weak in Western metas.
vs: Attack wide so the -1 might on one attacker matters less.
Pressure both battlefields so she can't just hold.
OGN-255.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Star Spring, named in this guide's game plan, is banned.

OGN-257.plan: Calm/Body unit-first midrange. Stack buffed units in one place, protected by Calm spells.
strengths: Buffed units are hard to remove cheaply.
weaknesses: Card draw.
vs: Don't overcommit big units into OGN-258.

OGN-259.plan: Calm/Chaos: snowball one unit (Stellacorn Herder, Irelia) using the Legend's move, protected by support spells.
vs: Remove the one unit he invests in.
strengths: Moves and protects key units.
weaknesses: Fragile units; Irelia does the same thing better.
OGN-259.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Stellacorn Herder, named in this guide's game plan, is banned.

OGN-261.plan: Calm/Order showdown deck. Stun enemy units so they deal no combat damage, then buff your own.
strengths: Specializes in showdowns; Calm protects units.
weaknesses: Little draw; weak to units sitting in base.
vs: Keep threats in base until you strike; play around stun.

OGS-021.plan: Mind/Order combo. Draw through most of the deck, then loop a recursion engine for unlimited energy and score out, often with repeated Time Warp.
strengths: Can win in one long turn once the loop is assembled.
weaknesses: Needs a nearly empty deck; loop pieces are vulnerable to gear removal.
Inconsistent results.
vs: Gear removal on the loop pieces.
Pressure early; the setup takes many turns.
Counter Time Warp (needs a counter that hits 4-power spells).

OGS-023.plan: Body/Order starter deck: go wide for the Legend's draw, or play buffs. Beginner-friendly, weakest competitively.
strengths: Cheap and simple.
weaknesses: Weakest legend competitively.
vs: Area damage and bounce.

SFD-181.plan: Fury/Mind Mech tribal. On the play, take a battlefield turn 2 with a Mech and snowball.
strengths: Fast start on the play.
weaknesses: Struggles on the draw; predictable.
vs: Contest early battlefields.

SFD-183.plan: Fury/Body conquer deck with Equipment (Assault). Conquer every turn and keep units alive.
strengths: Strong scoring; reached top cut of every early regional.
weaknesses: Narrow; reactive decks trouble it.
vs: Kill equipment and bounce equipped units.

SFD-189.plan: Calm/Mind gear aggro. Uses the Legend's power every turn for gear and moves OGN-091 around to score.
strengths: Won the Barcelona Regional Qualifier; strong draw.
weaknesses: Fragile if slowed early.
vs: Pressure early and kill gear.

SFD-193.plan: Calm/Body Equipment: move gear from a unit that acted to one that hasn't.
strengths: Hard-to-remove units.
weaknesses: Gear removal, bounce, thin draw.
vs: Gear removal and bounce.

SFD-201.plan: Mind/Order: rush to 5 points, then Gold fuels explosive turns.
strengths: Signature spell is removal or a closer.
weaknesses: Has struggled in the meta.
vs: Pressure early.

SFD-203.plan: Body/Chaos ramp into Dazzling Aurora and Elder Dragon, with Gold from recycled runes.
strengths: Sydney RQ finalist; strong Aurora synergy.
weaknesses: Elder Dragon struggles against wide boards of small units; gear removal.
vs: Go wide with small units; kill Dazzling Aurora.
SFD-203.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Dazzling Aurora, this deck's main ramp payoff in the guide, is banned.

SFD-205.plan: Body/Order flexible board deck: Baited Hook, Aurora gear, or unit midrange. Signature spell SFD-206 gets strong once she has extra runes.
strengths: Adaptable; hard to handle once ahead on runes.
weaknesses: Weak early game; gear versions die to gear removal.
vs: Pressure before she gains runes; gear removal for Aurora/Hook builds.
SFD-205.banImpact: Nov 23 bans: Baited Hook and Dazzling Aurora, two of the builds in the guide, are banned.

UNL-181.plan: Fury/Mind combo: cast 4+ cost spells to load the Legend, then win with Gutter Palace (4 cards in hand, 4 units at battlefields).
vs: Score early; kill Gutter Palace.
strengths: Can ignore the scoreboard.
weaknesses: Slow and rigid.

UNL-185.plan: Fury/Chaos disruptive value. Removal, Ambush units, Gold and discard to control both players' resources; converts with Fury removal when ahead, wins the long game otherwise.
strengths: Removal handles units of any size.
weaknesses: Inconsistent results.
vs: Force him to commit early before the value engine runs.

UNL-187.plan: Fury/Order burst. Readies a unit after big-excess-damage conquers. Unfocused per reviewers.

UNL-195.plan: Calm/Order pet and token typal; turns battlefields into Brush. Casual-strong.

UNL-203.plan: Body/Order hold XP. Gains XP on holds; draws with XP.

Legend:

RAD-149.note: Card roles, counters and sideboard ideas below are worked out from the card text and the four Orlando top-8 lists. Matchup numbers come from the sources shown. Treat the sideboard swaps as starting points to test, not a published plan.
engine: Riven's Legend only works at battlefields you already control: units you play there enter ready. Winning or holding the first battlefield is what turns the deck on, so your early turns are about getting and keeping one battlefield.

A ready unit is a resource. Exhausting it pays Blade of the Exile's Equip cost, and it triggers 'when I become exhausted' effects on Riven, Broken Blade (buff, then spend the buff to stun or ready her) and Reckless Innovator (Gold token or draw).

Calm keeps the plan safe: Defy, Not So Fast, Discipline and a hidden Zhonya's Hourglass protect the unit holding your battlefield. Chaos moves the opponent off it: Gust, Rebuke, Star-Crossed, Tideturner, Bedeviling Stranger and Switcheroo.
Astral Heron is the top end every list plays three of. Sitting at a battlefield, it discounts your second card each turn by 2 energy and 2 power, which lets you deploy and protect on the same turn.
core: 3 Blade of the Exile (your 3 Signature slots)
Battlefields: Star Spring and Rakelstake in all four lists, Emperor's Dais in three
Runes: 7 Chaos / 5 Calm in all four lists
mulligan: Keep hands that can put a unit on a battlefield by turn 2 and protect it: a 2-cost unit (Tideturner, Bedeviling Stranger, Scuttle Crab) plus Defy or Discipline is a solid keep.
Astral Heron and Baron Nashor are not opening-hand cards; send them back unless the rest of the hand is already strong.
Zhonya's Hourglass is good early because hiding it costs only 1 power and it saves the unit holding your battlefield.
Against fast decks (Rengar, Kha'Zix, Kai'Sa) favor cheap interaction; against slow decks (Jayce, Orianna, Mordekaiser) favor units and card flow (Stellacorn Herder, Scuttle Crab).
tips: Hold Defy for spells costing 4 energy or less with at most 1 power. It does not counter Falling Star, Punch First, Singularity or Time Warp (2+ power); Hush in the sideboard does.
Not So Fast counters spells and abilities that choose your unit or gear, so it covers single-target removal Defy can't reach.
Rebuke returns any unit at a battlefield to hand for 2 energy. Save it for the opponent's biggest investment (Elder Dragon, The Empyrean, Bloodscent Swarm).
Bedeviling Stranger only bounces when 4+ units are at that battlefield; it is strongest in the mirror and against wide boards.
Exhaust a fresh unit to equip Blade of the Exile instead of paying power, and sequence so Riven, Broken Blade's exhaust trigger stuns the attacker you care about.

The deck's Gold tokens (Reckless Innovator) and Battle Preparations (ready 2 runes when you show off a gear) let you keep reaction mana up on the opponent's turn. Plan your turn so you end with Defy or Not So Fast available.
sideboard: +4 might to your unit in combat with a Fury unit or chosen by a Fury spell. In against Kai'Sa, Rengar and Rek'Sai. Blanks Kai'Sa's Decree of Rage, Hextech Ray and Falling Star.
Kills a gear. In against Jayce (Dazzling Aurora, Gutter Palace, Platewyrm Egg), Orianna, Seraphine, Mordekaiser's Baited Hook, and the Riven mirror (Blade of the Exile).
A 4-might unit that kills a gear when you have 7+ runes. Second gear answer for Jayce and Orianna.
Counters spells with 2+ power: Falling Star, Singularity, Time Warp, Punch First, Rebuke. In against Kai'Sa, Kha'Zix, Rengar and the mirror.
Counters any spell and sends it back to hand, not the trash. Good against Kennen, whose Flow and replay cards want spells in the trash.
Deflect, and stuns units an opponent plays to her battlefield. Strong in the mirror and against decks that deploy to contested battlefields.
Can't be chosen by enemy spells or abilities outside combat. In against removal-heavy decks like Kai'Sa.
10-cost finisher that can't be targeted and gives your other units +2. In for slow games (Jayce, Orianna, mirrors that go long).

OGN-247.plan: The most common matchup, close to even (53% for Riven online across 187 matches; Riven won the Orlando top cut against Kai'Sa). Kai'Sa wins by removing your battlefield holder with cheap damage, then conquering with small units. Keep your holder protected: Defy hits Hextech Ray, Stupefy, Smoke Screen, Temporal Breach and Brittle Steel; Falling Star and Singularity need Hush or Not So Fast. Thousand-Tailed Watcher gives your units -3 when it lands, so don't count on might alone that turn. When Brynhir Thundersong is played, you can't play cards that turn, so set up protection (a hidden Zhonya's) the turn before.
watch: Decree of Rage (sideboard): 4 uncounterable damage to a Calm unit. Decree of Focus answers it.
Brittle Steel kills Blade of the Exile or Zhonya's.
Time Warp (10 energy, extra turn): Hush is your only counter.

VEN-155.plan: Coin flip: 49.5% online (99 matches), 51-49 for Kennen in early tournament data, and 3 Kennen made the Stuttgart top 8 next to 4 Riven. Kennen develops in bursts by playing cards from the trash and the top of the deck, then uses its Legend for Assault 2 on a conquer. Counter the cheap card-flow spells (Lightning Rush) and use Abandon on key spells so they go back to hand instead of feeding Flow. Bounce Nocturne and Kennen units off your battlefield on the turn they try to conquer.
watch: Rhasa the Sunderer gets cheaper with every card in their trash; expect it once their trash has 8-10 cards.
Tail-Cloaked Matriarch and Fizz replay units and spells from the trash.

RAD-149.plan: The mirror decided both big events (four of the Stuttgart top 8 and four of the Orlando top 8 were Riven). The first player to hold a battlefield gets ready units and the tempo. Bedeviling Stranger and Rebuke are at their best here because both sides stack units on battlefields. Save Defy or Hush for their Rebuke or Star-Crossed on your Astral Heron.
watch: Their Blade of the Exile: An Offer kills it.
Switcheroo can flip a combat with their Astral Heron.

VEN-149.plan: Sources disagree: early tournament data had Jayce at 64% against Riven, while 29 online matches had Riven winning 72%. Jayce ramps (Mobilize, Catalyst of Aeons) into Dazzling Aurora, which plays a free unit from the deck each turn, aiming for Elder Dragon. Gutter Palace is an alternate win: 4 cards in hand and 4 units at battlefields. Defy counters most of their spells (Mobilize, Catalyst, Dredge Up, Sabotage, Temporal Breach). Rebuke sends a 12-cost Elder Dragon back to hand for 2 energy. Bring gear removal for Aurora and Palace.
watch: Gutter Palace win check happens at the start of their Beginning Phase. Bounce one of their units or kill the gear before then.
Avalanche deals 3 to units in bases.

OGS-019.plan: Sources disagree: 67-33 for Yi in early tournament data, 58% for Riven across 45 online matches. Yi's lone defender gets +2 might, so bounce and moves are better than fighting. Rebuke and Star-Crossed ignore might; Gust only hits 3 might or less, which a buffed Yi defender may exceed. Blitzcrank, Impassive can drag a Yi unit to your battlefield.
watch: Note this Legend is banned in 2v2.

SFD-187.plan: Slightly unfavored: 46.9% online (36 matches); early tournament data had Rek'Sai winning against Riven. Her Legend triggers when she conquers, so hold your battlefield tight with Blitzcrank (Tank) and Zhonya's, and bounce her conquering unit. Fury removal is hers; Decree of Focus helps.
watch: Undertitan gives her other units +2 when played.

UNL-201.plan: Unfavored: 44.4% online (38 matches) and 57% for Kha'Zix in early tournament data. His deck wins combats with tricks (Punch First +5, Onslaught +6, Rampage) and Ambush units (Rengar, Trophy Hunter; Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror). Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror and Forbidding Waste punish a unit defending alone, so keep two units together. Hush counters Punch First (2 power); Defy handles Void Assault, Rampage and Onslaught.
watch: His own Vex, Apathetic stuns any unit you play while she's at a battlefield (anywhere, not just her battlefield), which cuts into your Legend's plan. Rebuke her (she has Deflect, so it costs 1 extra power).
The Good Stuff is a gear: An Offer kills it.

UNL-183.plan: Sources disagree: Riven 69% in early tournament data, Rengar 60% online (40 matches). Rengar wins the first showdowns with 3-might attackers and Ambush. Stop the early conquers with cheap bounce and stuns, and use Decree of Focus against his Fury units.
watch: Ambush units can join a showdown as a reaction; keep a counter or Discipline up when you defend.

RAD-153.plan: Favored: 57.4% online (69 matches). Evelynn hides cards and scores when she holds with a facedown card there. Bedeviling Stranger and Rebuke push her off battlefields; challenge her battlefields when you have protection ready.
watch: Evelynn, In Control scores an extra point when she holds with a facedown card at that battlefield.

RAD-145.plan: Favored: 61.9% online (63 matches). Her signature gear The Ball is protected, so aim gear removal at her other gears and unit removal at the gear while it is animated.
watch: SFD-084 gears ready her runes for reactions.

RAD-143.plan: Favored: 66.7% online (54 matches). Bounce his cheated-out champions with Rebuke or Star-Crossed and kill Baited Hook.
watch: Baited Hook (OGN-242) is the engine.

OGN-265.plan: Even: 52% online (54 matches). Viktor's 1-might tokens only score on empty battlefields, so keep both battlefields occupied when you can.
watch: UNL-153 lets Viktor conquer with two units in base.

SFD-195.plan: Unfavored online: 42.1% (24 matches). Irelia readies units and protects them with the same Calm spells you play. Bait counters before your key spell.
watch: Irelia, Fervent has Deflect.

UNL-199.plan: Favored: 61.3% online and 64% for Riven in early tournament data. Bouncing is better than killing because her Deathknells need units to die.

UNL-193.plan: Favored online: 55.6% (36 matches). Same Calm/Chaos colors; she holds one battlefield and bounces contesters. Pressure the second battlefield.
watch: Vex, Apathetic stuns any unit you play while she's at a battlefield, wherever you play it.

2v2.name: 2v2 (Magma Chamber)
rules: Two teams of two; teams alternate turns. Victory score is 11 shared team points, best of one.
Deck construction is the same as 1v1, but teammates can't play the same Legend or the same battlefields.
Each player brings 3 battlefields; the first player's are removed and the other three players each put one random battlefield into play.
Control is never shared: you can't move onto a battlefield your teammate occupies, move their units, or hide cards at their battlefields.
'Friendly' includes your teammate's units, so your buffs and ready effects can help them.
A battlefield can be scored only once per team per turn; one your teammate controlled at the start of your turn can't be scored by your team that turn.
Combat is always between exactly two players. A team loses if either player loses or concedes.
bans: Master Yi, Wuju Bladesman (Legend) is banned in 2v2 only, on top of the Standard ban list.
tips: Spread out: two players covering three battlefields is the core of the format.
Favor cheap units that can hold a battlefield alone over expensive top-end cards.
Games run long at 11 points; card draw and resilience matter more.

pairings.label: 2v2 team pairings covered in the Metafy guide for Radiance

ffa.name: Free-for-all: Skirmish (3 players) and War (4 players)
rules: Victory score 8, best of one, standard deck construction.
Three battlefields. In Skirmish each player contributes one; in War the first player's are removed and the other three contribute one each.
No teams. Combat is between exactly two players; a third player can't join an active fight.
The first player skips their first draw; the last player channels an extra rune.
tips: The public scoreboard makes the leader a target. Pace your points.
Spending a removal spell 1-for-1 helps the players you aren't fighting; card advantage and resilient threats matter more.
Holding is harder because you face several attackers; protection and recursion are worth more.

standard.name: Standard 1v1
rules: Best of three at most events, with a sideboard of up to 10 cards.
Victory score 8. One Legend, Chosen Champion plus 39 main-deck cards, 12 runes, 3 different battlefields.

combos.name: Fresh unit pays for the Blade
combos.how: A unit you play to a battlefield you control enters ready (Riven's Legend). Exhaust that newcomer to pay Blade of the Exile's Equip cost instead of spending power.

combos.name: Innovator engine
combos.how: Innovator enters ready at a battlefield you control without paying Accelerate. Exhaust it to equip the Blade; its exhaust trigger then gives a Gold gear token, or a draw for 1 Chaos power.

combos.name: 8-might Riven
combos.how: Exhaust a newcomer to equip the Blade on Riven. Each time she becomes exhausted, pick an option not used this turn: buff her, spend the buff to stun an enemy, or spend it to ready her. 4 might + 3 from the Blade + 1 buff = 8; spending the buff for a stun or a ready leaves 7.

combos.name: Herder draw
combos.how: Herder draws whenever it moves. Played to a battlefield you control it enters ready, so it can move back to base right away and draw.

combos.name: Star Spring double draw
combos.how: With Herder at Star Spring, play Scuttle Crab there (draw 1). Star Spring lets you move Herder to base for free, without exhausting it, so Herder draws too.

combos.name: Tideturner swap
combos.how: Your ready Astral Heron (or any big unit) sits on the battlefield you hold. Play Tideturner to base and swap them: Heron lands in base still ready and can make its standard move to attack the other battlefield, while Tideturner stays behind holding.

combos.name: Ride the Wind reset
combos.how: Ride the Wind moves a unit and readies it. On Herder it draws a card and leaves Herder ready for another move. On Riven, Broken Blade it readies her for a second exhaust trigger.

combos.name: Crab Switcheroo
combos.how: Switcheroo swaps the might of two units at the same battlefield this turn. Swap your 0-might Crab with their biggest unit: theirs drops to 0. Switcheroo costs 2 power, so Defy can't counter it (Hush can). It can also be hidden.

combos.name: Heron discount
combos.how: With Heron at a battlefield, your first card each turn makes your next card cost 2 energy and 2 power less. Lead with something cheap (Defy, Scuttle Crab), then Blitzcrank costs 3 energy and no power, and Star-Crossed or Switcheroo are nearly free.

combos.name: Blitzcrank pull
combos.how: Played to a battlefield you control, Blitzcrank enters ready and can move an enemy unit to that battlefield, pulling a defender out of their base or off their battlefield. When he holds, he returns to your hand to be replayed.

combos.name: Crab recycle
combos.how: Star-Crossed returns one friendly unit and one enemy unit to hand. Pick your Scuttle Crab as the friendly one and replay it to draw again.

combos.name: Crab scout
combos.how: Late game, send the Crab into an occupied battlefield. When it dies (Deathknell) the opponent reveals their hand, you can see their facedown cards this turn, and you gain 1 XP. Do it before a big turn.

combos.name: Dais Crab replay
combos.how: When you conquer Emperor's Dais, pay 1 energy to return a unit you control there (Scuttle Crab) to hand and get a 2-might Sand Soldier token. Replay the Crab later to draw again.

combos.name: Battle Preparations refund
combos.how: Show off a gear (from hand or in play) as you cast it: +2 might and ready 2 runes. That nearly pays for itself, so you keep Defy mana up.

combos.name: Zhonya's into an exhaust trigger
combos.how: When Zhonya's saves a unit it is recalled exhausted. If that unit is Riven, Broken Blade (or Reckless Innovator), becoming exhausted fires its trigger one more time.

combos.name: Deserter engine
combos.how: Deserter gets +1 might this turn every time another friendly unit becomes exhausted (paying Blade's Equip, attacking, Innovator). Once a turn, exhaust a friendly unit to ready a unit, for example Riven after she attacks.

combos.name: Hidden Stranger trap
combos.how: Hide Bedeviling Stranger at a battlefield you hold for 1 power. When 4 or more units pile in, play it for 0 energy as a reaction and return an enemy unit there to hand.

combos.name: Hillock ganking
combos.how: Units at Windswept Hillock have Ganking. A newcomer enters ready there and can move straight to the other battlefield.

combos.name: Back-Alley Bar might stack
combos.how: Units moving from Back-Alley Bar get +1 might this turn. Stack that with Deserter's exhaust bonus and Ride the Wind; the deck's author reports reaching 15+ might.

combos.name: Free Rebuke
combos.how: Rebuke costs 2 energy and 2 power. After your first card with Heron at a battlefield, it costs nothing.

combos.name: Gust self-bounce
combos.how: Gust returns a unit with 3 might or less to hand. Bounce your own Crab for 1 energy and replay it to draw, or bounce an enemy blocker.

combos.name: Treasure Hunter gold
combos.how: Treasure Hunter makes a Gold token whenever it moves; movement effects turn into extra power toward Heron and expensive spells.

combos.name: Valley buff for Riven
combos.how: Pay 1 energy when a unit is played to Valley of Idols to buff it. Riven enters with her buff already, so her first exhaust can spend it to stun or ready right away.

combos.name: Heron-discounted Possession
combos.how: With Heron at a battlefield, play any card first (Scuttle Crab, Battle Preparations, or a hidden card for 0 energy), then Possession costs 2 energy and 2 power less: 6 energy and 1 Chaos power. It takes an enemy unit at a battlefield for good and recalls it to your base.

combos.name: Hidden card as the free first card
combos.how: Hiding a card doesn't count as playing it, but playing it from facedown later does, for 0 energy. Flip a hidden Zhonya's or Bedeviling Stranger as your first card and your next card gets Heron's discount.

combos.name: Battle Preparations into Possession
combos.how: Battle Preparations (show off your Blade or Zhonya's) readies 2 runes, so it's nearly free, and it triggers Heron. Possession right after costs 6 energy and 1 Chaos power, about 7 runes on board.

combos.name: Steal an attacker in their showdown
combos.how: Heron's trigger is 'each turn' and Possession is an Action, so it works on their turn. When they attack Heron's battlefield, play a cheap reaction first (Not So Fast, Defy, Hush, Battle Preparations), then Possession on their biggest attacker: it's yours and leaves the fight.

combos.name: Not So Fast guards Heron
combos.how: Not So Fast counters any enemy spell or ability that chooses your unit, at any cost: Vengeance, Blast of Power, Drag Under, Hidden Blade, Harnessed Dragon, Solari Chief. On their turn it also counts as your first card for Heron's discount.

combos.name: Targon's Peak: counters up on their turn
combos.how: When you conquer Targon's Peak, 2 runes ready at the end of your turn, so you can spend your turn and still hold up Defy, Not So Fast or Hush on theirs.

combos.name: Crab scout before Possession
combos.how: Send Scuttle Crab into an enemy battlefield. When it dies they reveal their hand and you see their facedown cards this turn: if there's no Hush or other counter, cast Possession; if there is, bait it out first or wait a turn.

combos.name: Arm the stolen unit
combos.how: After Possession, equip Blade of the Exile to the stolen unit (+3 might and Ganking), or use Ride the Wind to move it out and ready it. Gear already on it stays under the opponent's control and returns to their base if the unit dies; a Weaponmaster unit (Azir's Sand Soldiers, Ornn, Riven, Shattered) can move it back.

combos.name: Heron first, then a free Battle Preparations
combos.how: Play Astral Heron as your first card of the turn, to a battlefield you control. Heron counts its own play: it's at the battlefield when it finishes resolving, so your next card costs 2 energy and 2 power less. Battle Preparations (normally 2 energy) is then free. Show off a gear (Blade of the Exile or Zhonya's, from hand or in play) and it readies 2 of the runes Heron used, so you end the turn with Heron on the board, +2 might on a unit and 2 runes open. Two ready runes pay for Defy, Hush or Not So Fast on their turn (exhaust both, recycle one or two for the power), which is your rule for protecting Heron.

OGN-247.hold: Keep Zhonya's hidden on the unit holding your battlefield. Don't stack your whole board in one spot before Thousand-Tailed Watcher, which gives your units -3 when it lands.
watch: Removal then conquer: Hextech Ray or Falling Star on your holder, then a small unit takes the battlefield.
Brynhir Thundersong: you can't play cards that turn, so set up the turn before.
Time Warp (10 energy, extra turn): only Hush counters it.

side.why: Hush and Not So Fast are already in your main deck for Falling Star, Singularity, Time Warp and her targeted removal. Decree saves small units from her Fury damage; her units are small, so Switcheroo does less.

mull.keep: Two-drop plus Defy or Zhonya's. After sideboarding, Decree of Focus is a fine keep.
mull.ship: Astral Heron on the play (keep it on the draw).

VEN-155.hold: Save Star-Crossed or Possession for the turn Kennen goes for a conquer with Assault 2.
watch: Nocturne and Rhasa come back from the trash; Rhasa costs 1 less per card in his trash, so expect it once his trash has 8 to 10 cards.
Lightning Rush and Trifarian Captain dig for cards cheaply; Defy counters them.
His Legend gives Assault 2 when he plays cards from anywhere other than his hand.
Abandon (1 main, 1 sideboard) can counter Possession; Defy counters Abandon.

side.why: Ryan's plan: Discipline wins showdowns against his Assault 2 attacks and Deserter races him before his trash fills; his units are small, so Switcheroo does less. His 2-power spells (Rebuke, Switcheroo) target your units, so Not So Fast covers them; Hush is only needed for Imperial Decree from his sideboard.
side.cond: If he shows Imperial Decree, bring 2 Hush back in for game 3 (it's the only counter for it).

mull.keep: Two-drop plus Reckless Innovator or Defy; pressure early.
mull.ship: Astral Heron. Keep Possession; Rhasa is the unit you'll want to steal.

VEN-149.hold: Hold Possession for Elder Dragon or his biggest unit. Hold Bedeviling Stranger for when Gutter Palace is close (4 of his units at battlefields).
watch: Dazzling Aurora plays a free unit from the top of his deck at the end of each turn.
Elder Dragon (12 cost) lets any damage kill your units.
Gutter Palace wins at the start of his turn with exactly 4 cards in hand and 4 units at battlefields.

side.why: Offer kills Dazzling Aurora, Gutter Palace or Platewyrm Egg. Hush in your main deck already covers his 2+ power spells.

mull.keep: Slow matchup: Stellacorn Herder, Scuttle Crab and Astral Heron are all keeps; An Offer after sideboarding.

RAD-149.hold: Keep Not So Fast or Defy up for their Star-Crossed, Rebuke or Possession on your Astral Heron.
watch: Their Riven with the Blade reaches 8 might.
Switcheroo flips combat in their favor (Hush counters it, Defy doesn't).
Their hidden Bedeviling Stranger when you stack 4+ units.

side.why: Four gear answers for their Blade and Zhonya's: Offer, plus Disarming Rake, a 2-might unit that kills a gear when played (Emperor's Dais or Star-Crossed can return it to replay). Hush in your main deck counters their Rebuke, Switcheroo, Possession and Hush. Rake's kill is an ability, so their Not So Fast can counter it.

mull.keep: Two-drop plus Bedeviling Stranger or Blade; being first to hold a battlefield decides the mirror.

UNL-201.hold: Hold Hush for Punch First and keep Switcheroo for after he pumps a unit (swap its might with your Crab).
watch: Punch First (+5) and Onslaught win combats.
Ambush units join showdowns: Rengar, Trophy Hunter and Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror.
Forbidding Waste and Mutating Horror punish a unit defending alone.
His Vex, Apathetic stuns any unit you play while she's at a battlefield, wherever you play it.

side.why: Hush in your main deck covers Punch First. Discipline helps you win the early fights his Ambush units start.

mull.keep: Two units early so you never defend alone; Discipline for combat.

SFD-195.hold: Hold Possession for Irelia, Fervent or her biggest readied unit, ideally after Heron's discount or in her showdown. Bait her counter with a cheaper spell first.
watch: She readies her units and protects them with the same Calm spells you play.
Irelia, Fervent has Deflect: targeting her costs 1 extra power.

side.why: No swap needed by default: Possession is in your main deck for Irelia, Fervent and her readied units, and Hush is in the main deck for any 2+ power spell.
side.cond: Targeting Irelia, Fervent costs 1 extra power (Deflect).

mull.keep: Two-drop plus card flow (Stellacorn Herder, Scuttle Crab) and Defy.

UNL-183.hold: Keep Discipline or Decree of Focus for his first showdowns.
watch: 3-might attackers win the early showdowns.
Ambush units join combats as reactions.
Punch First.

side.why: Decree and Discipline win the early fights against his Fury attackers; Hush in your main deck covers Punch First. Your 7- and 8-cost cards are too slow against aggro.

mull.keep: Two-drop plus cheap interaction; Decree after sideboarding.
mull.ship: Astral Heron. In game 1 your rule keeps Possession; for games 2 and 3 it's sided out.

OGS-019.hold: Don't fight his lone defender head-on; move or bounce it.
watch: A lone defender gets +2 might.
Punch First.

side.why: No swap needed by default: Hush in your main deck counters Punch First, and Star-Crossed and Possession handle his lone defender.
side.cond: Bring in 2 Discipline for 2 Ride the Wind if his early fights are beating you.

mull.keep: Star-Crossed with a two-drop; moving or bouncing beats fighting.
mull.ship: Battle Preparations or extra copies of reactions. Keep Possession.

SFD-187.hold: Keep Zhonya's on the unit holding your battlefield; she wants to conquer every turn.
watch: Her Legend reveals the top 2 cards and plays one when she conquers.
Falling Star and Hidden Blade on your holder.

side.why: Decree blanks her Fury removal; Not So Fast in your main deck stops Falling Star and Hidden Blade on your units, and Hush covers Falling Star too.

mull.keep: Two-drop plus Zhonya's; contest her early conquers.

OGN-269.hold: Keep Defy up when you cast Possession: his Repulse (1 energy + 1 power) counters a spell that targets his unit, and Defy counters Repulse. Hold Hush for Punch First (+5 might). Don't count on combat kills of a buffed unit: his legend recalls it instead of letting it die. Bounce and Possession aren't deaths, so they get around it.
watch: The Boss (legend): when a buffed unit would die, he pays 1 power and exhausts the legend to recall it to base instead; the legend readies when he conquers.
Sabotage (1 energy + 1 power): he sees your hand and recycles a non-unit card, like Possession or a counter. Cards hidden on the board are safe from it. Defy counters it.
Repulse: counters your spell or ability aimed at his unit, including Possession and Star-Crossed. Defy counters Repulse.
Punch First (+5) and Call to Glory (+3, free if he spends a buff) win combats; Hush counters Punch First, Defy counters Call to Glory.
Challenge (fight) and Hidden Blade (kill) on your units: Not So Fast or Defy.
Vi, Peacekeeper: Ambush, stuns one of your units when she attacks.

Fae Dragon (7 might, buffs up to four units) and Sett, Kingpin (5-might Tank, +1 per buffed unit there) are the Possession targets. Fiora, Victorious gets Deflect at 5+ might (+1 power to target her).

side.why: Claude's suggestion, not tested: his deck wins by fighting with buffs and pump spells, so Discipline helps you win early showdowns. Ride the Wind is the card your plan needs least here.
side.cond: An Offer You Can't Refuse kills Arena Bar (his buff engine), but he runs only 2, so it's probably not worth the slots.

mull.keep: Two-drop plus Defy (it covers Sabotage, Repulse, Call to Glory and Challenge). Keep Possession for Fae Dragon or Kingpin.
mull.ship: Astral Heron on the play if the hand has no early plays.

VEN-139.hold: Hold Not So Fast for Falling Star or Back Off on your Heron; Hush also counters Falling Star (2 power).
watch: Falling Star (3 damage, twice) and Shuriken Flip (2 damage, then it moves a unit) aimed at your battlefield holder.
Hidden Back Off stuns your attacker, and a hidden Mischievous Marai deals 2 to one of your units when it lands at her battlefield.
Her Legend pulls her best unit back to base from a fight she's losing, so your attacks rarely trade one for one.
Akali, Deadly Weapon pings 1 (2 once Empowered) when she moves.
Blitzcrank, Impassive pulls one of your units onto his battlefield; she also runs Zhonya's and Astral Heron.

side.why: Decree of Focus gives +4 to a unit fighting her Fury units or chosen by her Fury spells (Falling Star, Shuriken Flip). Hush and Not So Fast in your main deck already cover Falling Star.

mull.keep: Two-drop plus Not So Fast or Defy; her early damage goes at your first holder.
mull.ship: Ride the Wind, Battle Preparations, extra reactions.

UNL-193.hold: Hold Hush for Switcheroo and Rebuke (both 2 power); Not So Fast also stops them on your units. Possession on Vex costs 1 extra power (Deflect).
watch: Vex, Apathetic stuns any unit you play while she's at a battlefield, wherever you play it. Remove or steal her before your big turn.
Hidden cards everywhere: Switcheroo, Back Off, Tornado Warrior, Evelynn, Gutter Guardian, Zhonya's and Edge of Night.
Holding a battlefield draws her a card (her Legend).
Rebuke and Switcheroo on your units; Hunting Blind pulls one of your units onto its battlefield.
Her own Astral Herons and Steel Paws (+7 once Empowered).

side.why: Offer kills Zhonya's, Boots of Swiftness, Edge of Night, Sterak's Gage or Hunting Blind. Hush in your main deck covers Switcheroo and Rebuke.

mull.keep: Two-drop plus Hush or Not So Fast.

OGN-265.hold: Keep Defy for Cull the Weak (2 energy + 1 power) and Hush for Imperial Decree (5 energy + 2 power); Not So Fast stops Hidden Blade and Wages of Pain on Heron.
watch: Recruits every turn: its Legend makes a 1-might Recruit, and Viktor, Leader adds one whenever another of its units dies.
Cull the Weak makes each player kill a unit: it sacrifices a Recruit while you lose a real unit.
Hidden Blade and Wages of Pain on your holder.
Imperial Decree: any unit that takes damage that turn dies.
Sprite Burst and Sprite Fountain make 3-might Temporary Sprites that die at the start of its next turn; Thousand-Tailed Watcher gives your units -3.

side.why: Its units are mostly 1-might tokens, so Switcheroo with your Crab does little. Discipline wins the fights against Sprites and keeps a unit alive through Wages of Pain.

mull.keep: Two-drop plus Defy (Cull the Weak) or Not So Fast.

UNL-199.hold: Hold Possession for Karthus, Eternal or Harnessed Dragon: stealing a unit doesn't trigger its Deathknell, and bouncing it (Star-Crossed) doesn't either.
watch: Deathknell units pay out when they die: Honest Broker (Gold), Soaring Scout and Black Rose Dignitary (a rune), Watchful Sentry (a card), Ruined Rex (4 damage to your unit), Rift Herald (a free unit from hand).
Karthus, Eternal makes every Deathknell trigger twice. Remove or steal him first.

mullNote.base: Your rule: keep if you have a two-drop unit (Scuttle Crab first). No two-drop: always send back 2. Send back duplicates except Stellacorn Herder and Blade of the Exile. why.Riven - Broken Blade: Riven was 43% of decks at the European Regional Championship with 3 of the top 4. Riot: a guaranteed turn-two play that conquers while risking nothing.
why.Zhonya's Hourglass: Protects strong units from removal, can be hidden to dodge gear removal, and is especially strong with Astral Heron.
why.Stellacorn Herder: An unlimited reward for movement effects; replaces itself right away in Riven and gives Calm decks draw. Riot expects it to get worse over time.
why.Rhasa the Sunderer: A strong payoff for filling the trash, which Kennen does well; costs 0 energy and can be recurred.
why.Brynhir Thundersong: Played in the opponent's Beginning phase it can lock them out of playing cards on their turn; with blink effects it's very strong removal.
why.Dazzling Aurora: Pushes energy-ramp and Body decks into one path to win; its threats are too dangerous on one card.
why.Baited Hook: Cheats out free high-cost units with limited search and checks might rather than energy cost; banned early ahead of upcoming Legacy cards.
why.Emperor's Dais: Removes the risk of conquering, which promotes no-risk conquers; especially strong with Riven.
why.Star Spring: Same reason as Emperor's Dais; Riot compares it to the earlier-banned Reaver's Row.
why.Nocturne - Horrifying: An early zero-energy play that costs no card when found off a reveal; Riot expects more 'look at the top of your deck' cards to make it worse.

banSchedule.note: No cards were unbanned or restricted. Riot says Kennen and Yasuo are not banned in 2v2 and no extra 2v2 bans are being made. These bans don't apply to competitive events in Korea or Traditional Chinese regions until Radiance releases there.

RAD-145.plan: Orianna (computer): Calm/Mind gear control. At the start of each Main Phase it pays 1 energy to turn its biggest gear into a unit (might = energy cost): The Ball (5, Deploy, Ganking, draws or deals 2 to enemies when played or moved) and Resplendent Rostrum (8). Cheap Poros and Lecturing Yordle hold early; Stupefy, Defy, Wages of Pain, Deadly Flourish and Singularity handle threats; Orianna, Mechanical Marvel at a battlefield makes gear cheaper.

UNL-181.plan: Jhin (computer): Fury/Mind big-spell control. Spells it spends 4+ energy on (Curtain Call, Time Warp, Unchecked Power, Singularity) are banished with Jhin; at four it gets them back in the trash, channels 4 runes and draws. A 4-energy spell also lets Jhin, Meticulous Killer cost 1 Mind power. Plundering Poro, Noxus Hopeful and Forecaster hold early; Stupefy, Deadly Flourish, Rocket Barrage and Curtain Call control the board.

UNL-185.plan: Pyke (computer): Chaos/Fury bounce value. The legend pays 1 energy to return a friendly unit at a battlefield to hand for a Gold, saving a dying unit or replaying a 'When you play me' unit (Ezreal, Prodigy draws; Tail-Cloaked Matriarch, Kai'Sa). Pyke, Returned hides and makes Gold when enemies die; Ripper's Bay channels a rune on every return. Falling Star, Cleave and Existential Dread win fights; Kharox closes.

OGN-267.plan: Miss Fortune (computer): Body/Chaos gear ramp into dragons. Treasure Trove, Scryer's Bloom, Pack of Wonders and Dazzling Aurora build card and rune advantage; Mobilize and Catalyst of Aeons ramp toward Elder Dragon and Baron Nashor, with The Harrowing and Heedless Resurrection bringing them back.
